clue.text: An old writer is rather slow

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, the medieval Italian poet

explanation.surface: A veteran author has slowed down with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderate, walking pace, somewhat slow without dragging.

clue.text: Poor race time for this stretch

indicators.note: a poor version is a badly made one, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters to rearrange
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An athlete clocks a disappointing time on this section of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area of land measured in acres, so a stretch of ground.

clue.text: Stop the race to perdition!

parts.note: to dam is to stop a flow
a race or people is a nation

explanation.surface: An angry cry to halt the race and send it to hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdition is eternal punishment in hell, the same fate as damnation in Christian theology.

clue.text: A girl of canny disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A shrewd young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy is a familiar female first name, so it can stand for one particular girl.

clue.text: Steps one might well take to make getting up easier

definitions.text: Steps one might well take to make getting up easier

parts.note: surface reading: measures a person might sensibly adopt
setter's reading: actual stairs, a moving flight that carries people
surface: rising from bed; setter's: going to a higher floor

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like advice on waking in the morning; the 'steps' are a moving staircase and 'getting up' is going upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a moving staircase whose powered steps carry people up between floors with no effort.

clue.text: Male champions become bullies

parts.note: males are men
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: Successful sportsmen turn into thugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to threaten or intimidate them, which is what a bully does to a victim.

clue.text: Capital agency!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the method by which something is done

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes it read like praise for a business; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both wealth or financial resources and the instrument or method through which an end is achieved.

clue.text: Up-to-date business course

parts.note: up-to-date means new
a market is trade or business

explanation.surface: A modern commercial training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business course' sounds like a class; the course is a racecourse. Newmarket in Suffolk is the home of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a famous English racecourse, so it is one example of a course for horse racing.

clue.text: Pause when speaking at this point

definitions.text: Pause when speaking at this point

parts.words: Pause when speaking at this point
parts.note: surface reading: an instruction to stop talking for a moment here
setter's reading: a punctuation mark in writing that tells a reader aloud where to take a short breath

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a stage direction; the clue is describing the punctuation mark that marks such a short pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma marks a slight break in a sentence, the place where a reader naturally takes a brief pause.

clue.text: Settling with evil potentate

parts.note: sin is wickedness
a king is a powerful ruler

explanation.surface: Coming to terms with a wicked tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinking and settling both describe something gradually going down, as a building subsides into soft ground.

clue.text: An Italian's unchurched love affair

indicators.note: to be unchurched is to have the church taken away, so the abbreviation for church is struck out

parts.note: a romance is a love affair

explanation.surface: An Italian has an affair outside the blessing of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) is removed from the end of ROMANCE, leaving ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman is a native of Rome, the capital of Italy, so one example of an Italian person.

clue.text: The cleaner exhibits charm now — a change!

indicators.note: a change tells us the preceding letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange, the dash ignored

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady is suddenly being delightful, which makes a nice change.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a woman employed to do domestic cleaning, an old British term for a cleaning lady.

clue.text: The bloomer of a witless pushover

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over means turned upside down, so in a down-reading sense the letters go backwards

parts.note: witless means silly
the first part, push, means ram; the rest of the word is the turnaround signal (printed push-over)

explanation.surface: A bloomer is a foolish mistake, here made by some gullible soft touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushover' looks like one word for a gullible person, but the printed push-over splits in two, and only the witless push is turned round, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is something that blooms, a flower, and the amaryllis is a bulb grown for its large trumpet-shaped flowers.

clue.text: A violin-making family could appear a dull one

parts.note: taken as written
mat (also matt) describes a dull, non-shiny finish
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A family of instrument makers might come across as rather boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati were a family of Cremona craftsmen who made celebrated violins in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Last English eleven a good man formed

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for English
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a cricket team is an eleven
a saint is a good man, abbreviated St

explanation.surface: The final England cricket team was put together around one fine player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective about the team, but it is the verb: to last is to go on being.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue to be, to endure or survive, which is what existing means.

clue.text: Oral distress over article about a church

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around another

parts.note: over and too both mean excessively
the definite article
taken as written
the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a newspaper piece about a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral' suggests something spoken; it means of the mouth. 'Over' here means excessively, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothache is pain in a tooth, a kind of suffering located in the mouth.

clue.text: Flashy second

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sparkling, giving off little flashes of light
second meaning: a very brief moment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashy' looks like a judgement on someone's taste, and 'second' like a position; both are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinkling describes light flickering in brief bursts, and as a noun means an instant, a split moment of time.

clue.text: A countryman may be care-lined

indicators.note: may be suggests the following letters could become something else when reordered

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rural worker's face is often lined with worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' suggests a rustic; here it means a native of a particular country.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a citizen of Iceland, so a fellow countryman of other people from that nation.

clue.text: Sick jokes occasioning bad feeling

parts.note: sick means ill
jokes are humour

explanation.surface: Tasteless jokes cause resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick jokes' reads as one phrase about bad taste; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill humour is a bad mood or irritable temper, a state of grumpy, sour feeling.

clue.text: The crowd not in favour of the hunt?

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
to course is to hunt hares with hounds by sight

explanation.surface: The public are against fox-hunting, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a throng of people gathered together, as well as the open space where such a gathering forms.

clue.text: Many being examined in competition

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
something being examined is on test

explanation.surface: Lots of candidates sit exams in a competitive setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving C (a hundred) is a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a competition, an event in which rivals strive to win.

clue.text: In part a lush grassy slope, in part a scree

definitions.text: grassy slope, in part a scree

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the following words is used, the answer sitting within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word, the next, and the start of another

explanation.surface: A description of a hillside, green in some places and stony in others.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In part' does double duty, and the second 'in part' belongs to the definition: a talus can be partly grassed and partly loose rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A talus is a sloping heap of rock fragments at the foot of a cliff, or more generally any slope, so scree in part.

clue.text: Look at the paper, sweating

parts.note: to see is to look at
a page is a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: Someone nervously reads the newspaper, perspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweating' is used in the sense of a wall or pipe sweating, letting liquid through.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is moisture slowly oozing out, a fair if loose match for liquid coming through as sweat does through skin.

clue.text: Point taken by the prime minister at one time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the four cardinal points of the compass

definitions.text: the prime minister at one time
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Lord ..., British prime minister when the American colonies were lost

explanation.surface: A former premier concedes a point in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: North is a compass bearing, and Frederick, Lord North, led the British government from 1770 to 1782.

clue.text: Note on the first woman magistrate

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Eve, the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A memo about the first female judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was the chief magistrate of an English town or district in Anglo-Saxon and medieval times.

clue.text: Change made if teams turn out badly

indicators.note: out badly means emerging all wrong, so the letters before it come out in a muddled order

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A manager vows to make changes if the sides perform poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out badly' reads as one phrase meaning fail, but 'turn' belongs with the fodder and only 'out badly' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute is to change something from one form or substance into another, as alchemists hoped to do with metals.

clue.text: The end of most requests for work

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: final letter of the word
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Applications for jobs are mostly over.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done, jobs assigned to someone.

clue.text: Writing a few last words up when fit

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom of the grid upward

parts.note: MS, short for manuscript, is a piece of writing
taken as written
a postscript is a few words added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An author jots a few final words once healthy again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' suggests healthy; it is the noun, a sudden seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary convulsion or fit, as of coughing or muscular contraction.

clue.text: Drilled or cut without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: excised means cut out
the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A soldier was trained, or a passage was removed without any pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'promptly'; here 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the word for cut wraps around the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercised means put through drills or physical training, as troops or athletes are trained by repeated practice.

clue.text: A painter receiving an honour and bouquet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An artist gets a royal honour and a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers handed to the painter; it is the wine-taster's sense, a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is the characteristic scent of a wine, and an aroma is a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Attic hero uses the revised version

indicators.note: a revised version is a rewritten one, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An ancient hero relies on an updated edition of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' means of Attica, the region around Athens, not a loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the legendary king of Athens who slew the Minotaur, the chief hero of Attica.

clue.text: Servicemen's code for contrition?

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
Morse code, signalled in dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Soldiers have a rule of conduct for owning up to wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong one has done, very close in meaning to contrition.
